# marcus: the metrics he chose

From sweep 3 (see `../METRICS-THEY-CHOSE.md`). Kept here verbatim so the
corpus carries his units, not the schema's. Pinned attribution
(`../.scratch/ARCS.md`, SWEEP-3 METRIC ATTRIBUTION): these five items belong
to marcus only.

- **A private segment head-to-head with a friend, three local segments** -
  "I would never admit to him that I know the score. I know the score." No
  schema field holds a segment rivalry; it stays here, in prose, the way
  nora's magpie count and segment ledger stay in hers.
- **Whether the kids came and watched, and which one.** Both Alfie and Rosie
  came to the 2029-04 PB and the 2029-10 DNF in this world's telling. The
  two are different things to him - and the schema has no way to say which
  child stood where. `sessions.with` records a child running ALONGSIDE him
  (the parkrun rows); it has no field for a child watching him race alone.
  See `FINDINGS.md` and expectation `marcus-E-spectator`.
- **Mornings out the door before the house woke.** Most of his training runs
  start before 08:00 - genuinely true, and visible in `sessions.start_time`
  most of the time, but the FEELING of beating the house awake is not the
  same fact as the clock time, and only he counts it.
- **Weeks I didn't drop a planned session even though the week was a
  write-off.** No schema home; a session either happened or didn't, and
  nothing here holds "the week was hard and I still didn't skip."
- **Phone-free conversations with Claire.** Relational, binary - did they,
  not how long. No schema home for it, the same way rachel's "did we walk
  together" and derek's "sat-down-together evenings with Pam" stay in
  theirs.

## What he explicitly does not want

A number for the segment rivalry - naming it to anyone, let alone tracking
it, would ruin the point of it being private. He is fine with the marathon
times being public and precise; the segment ledger and the "which kid
watched" count are the two things he keeps to himself.
